back.W3: Save what you type again and again, then tap it on the keyboard in any app
back.W5: Copy the image you saved with one tap and paste it anywhere
back.W7: No account or internet; cutlings sync only through your own iCloud
back.A2: Turn on Cutling in Settings, then return here
back.A5: Video of the Settings steps: tap Keyboards, turn on Cutling, turn on Allow Full Access and tap Allow
back.F2: Cutling types your text without it
back.F4: Full Access lets the keyboard copy a saved image and add what you copied
back.F5: Data does not leave the iPhone
back.F6: Cutling has no account, does not connect to the internet, and does not read what you type
back.F8: iOS shows the very same warning for every keyboard that asks, regardless of what it does
back.T4: Tap and hold the %@ key below, choose Cutling, then tap Try Me
back.T5: Cutling typed this. You are ready
back.N2: Spaces to fill, and more room
back.N3: More room, and every key types
back.N5: Add a blank space or today's date from the editor, and fill it each time you type a cutling
back.N7: Save up to %1$@ texts and %2$@ images
back.N9: Tap a formatted cutling and it types like the others; hold to copy the format
back.N12: Hold the globe key on your keyboard, then choose Cutling
back.N14: Tap a cutling and it is typed where you are writing
back.N16: Send text, links or images to Cutling from any app
back.TU1: While typing, tap the curly-brackets button to leave a blank space to fill each time you use it. Tap Next to skip

notes: Uses the file's Mipangilio, Kibodi, Ufikiaji Kamili, Ruhusu Ufikiaji Kamili, ubao wa kunakili. Cutling kept as an unchanged noun, no plural prefix. Swahili words are longer, so several lines are short paraphrases.
